I couldn't find a bug in `slugify` here, so I haven't changed anything. Your `django/utils/text.py:481` matches upstream Django line for line, and the template filter at `django/template/defaultfilters.py:268` just calls it.

I couldn't run Django's test suite because `asgiref` isn't installed in this environment. Instead I ran a copy of the function on some sample titles. These are the cases most likely to look "mangled" to your users:

| Input | Default output | With `allow_unicode=True` |
|---|---|---|
| `Straße Ærø` | `strae-r` | `straße-ærø` |
| `你好 World` | `world` | `你好-world` |
| `Привет мир` | `''` (empty) | `привет-мир` |
| `a & b` | `a-amp-b` | `a-amp-b` |
| `C++ / C#` | `c-c` | `c-c` |

That points to three likely causes:

1. **Non-Latin text gets dropped.** By default, slugify only keeps ASCII characters, so `ß`, `Æ`, Chinese, Cyrillic and so on disappear, and a title can end up with an empty slug. If your users write in other languages, the fix is in your code: call `slugify(title, allow_unicode=True)` and make sure the model field is `SlugField(allow_unicode=True)`.
2. **The text was already HTML-escaped.** If titles are escaped before they're slugified, `&` turns into `amp`. The fix is to slugify the raw text, not the escaped version.
3. **Symbols are stripped on purpose.** `C++` and `C#` both become `c`, so different titles can get the same slug. That's how slugify is meant to work. If it matters, you'd need your own mapping, such as `+` → `plus`.

Changing Django's own `slugify` in this repo would change it for every caller, so the fix belongs where your site calls it. I don't have your site's code or any of the bad URLs. Could you send one or two real titles with the URLs they produced, and point me to where your app calls `slugify`? Then I can make the fix there.
